label: Hedge Trimming
title: Hedge Trimming
description: Hedge trimming and cutting across Newquay, Truro, St Austell, Bodmin, and the wider Cornwall area. I handle everything from a quick tidy on a low box hedge to a full reset on overgrown leylandii. Neat shapes, clean lines, and a consistent finish every time. Cornwall's mild climate and longer growing season mean hedges here can quickly get out of hand if they are not kept on top of, so sensible timing and regular cuts make all the difference. Prices start from £5 per metre for smaller hedges and go up to around £15 per metre for taller or thicker growth.

included.label: What's included
included.title: A clean shape that stays looking tidy
included.description: I focus on a neat, even finish with sensible shaping that suits the hedge type. Every trim includes clearing up around the base so you are not left with a mess. I will also advise on the best time to cut for your particular species, because getting the timing right keeps hedges healthy and thick rather than thin and leggy. I hold a chainsaw licence and public liability insurance, so larger or more awkward jobs are covered properly.

items.title: Shaping & trimming
items.description: I cut clean, straight lines that make hedges look intentional and well kept. Whether you want a formal squared-off shape or something a bit softer and more natural, I will match the style to what suits your property and the hedge species.

items.title: Height & width control
items.description: Keeping height and width under control prevents hedges from encroaching on paths, driveways, or neighbouring properties. I can reduce hedges that have got too big over the years, though the best time for a hard cut-back is late winter before nesting season starts. For regular maintenance trims, I keep the shape consistent so the hedge thickens up rather than getting thin at the base.

items.title: Problem area tidy-up
items.description: Uneven corners, lopsided sections, and gaps where growth has not filled in properly. These are common in Cornwall where salt winds near the coast can damage one side of a hedge more than the other. I will tidy up problem areas and advise on whether any replanting or infill would help in the long run.

items.title: Season-aware approach
items.description: Different hedge species need cutting at different times of year. Leylandii and similar conifers need a minimum of two cuts per year, typically in late spring and late summer. Beech, laurel, and privet are more forgiving and often only need one or two trims. I will recommend a schedule that keeps your hedge healthy and looking its best throughout the year.

items.title: Green waste removal (optional)
items.description: All hedge clippings and trimmings can be collected and removed from site. Green waste removal is £10 per dumpy bag. I am a licensed waste carrier, so disposal is done properly and legally. For smaller trims the waste cost is minimal, and I will always let you know the likely amount before starting.

items.title: Ongoing maintenance option
items.description: Regular seasonal trims are the easiest way to keep hedges looking sharp year-round. I offer repeat visits at sensible intervals based on the hedge type, usually two to three times per year. This prevents the kind of heavy overgrowth that costs more to deal with later and keeps the hedge thicker and healthier.

plans.label: Options
plans.title: Choose a trim that matches your needs

I offer everything from a quick tidy to restore clean lines through to a full reset on hedges that have been left for a year or more. Most hedges benefit from two to three cuts per year, and I can set up a regular schedule so you do not have to remember to book each time.

cards.title: Light tidy trim
cards.description: A quick pass to tidy up the outline and restore clean edges. Ideal for hedges that are already in reasonable shape and just need freshening up. Works well as a between-seasons touch-up to keep things neat.

cards.title: Shape and refine
cards.description: A more thorough trim that evens out the shape, corrects any lopsided growth, and leaves a sharper finish. This is what most customers go for when their hedge needs more than a light tidy but has not been left too long.

cards.title: One-off reset
cards.description: For hedges that have been neglected or left to grow unchecked for a season or more. I will cut back hard to restore a manageable shape and advise on what to expect with regrowth. Common with leylandii and laurel that have got too tall or wide.

cards.title: Regular maintenance
cards.description: Two to three scheduled visits per year keeps hedges thick, even, and looking sharp without the need for bigger reset jobs. I will remind you when each trim is due so nothing gets missed. This is the most cost-effective approach for keeping hedges in good shape over time.

faq.label: FAQs
faq.title: Quick answers
faq.description: If you don't see your question here, just get in touch.

items.question: How often should hedges be trimmed?
items.answer: Most hedges need 2 to 3 cuts per year to stay healthy and looking sharp. Fast-growing species like leylandii need a minimum of 2 cuts, typically in late spring and late summer, to stop them getting out of hand. Slower-growing hedges such as beech or laurel can often get away with 1 to 2 cuts per year. Cornwall's mild coastal climate means hedges tend to grow for longer than in other parts of the UK, so keeping on top of them is important. I can advise on the right schedule for your specific hedge type when I come out for a quote.

items.question: Can you reduce the height or width?
items.answer: Yes, I can reduce hedges in both height and width. This is common when hedges have been left to grow unchecked for a season or two, or when they are encroaching on paths, driveways, or neighbouring properties. The best time for a hard reduction is late winter or early spring before nesting season, though lighter shaping can be done at other times of year. I always check for nesting birds before starting any work. If a hedge needs a significant reduction, I will let you know what to expect in terms of regrowth so there are no surprises.

items.question: Do you remove hedge clippings?
items.answer: Yes, I remove all hedge clippings and leave the site tidy. Green waste removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag, which covers transport and disposal. I am a licensed waste carrier, so you can be confident everything is disposed of properly and legally. For smaller trims the waste cost is minimal. I will always give you a clear idea of likely waste costs before starting the job.

items.question: Do you do one-off trims?
items.answer: Yes, one-off hedge trims are no problem at all. Plenty of customers get in touch because a hedge has got away from them or they need it tidied before selling a property. Hedge trimming is priced at £5 to £15 per metre depending on the size of the hedge and how many sides need cutting. I am happy to come out, take a look, and give you a straightforward quote. If you then decide you would like regular seasonal trims going forward, I can set that up too.

items.question: Do you cover my area?
items.answer: I am based near Newquay and cover a good chunk of Cornwall, including Truro, St Austell, Bodmin, Padstow, Perranporth, and St Ives. If you are within that area, I can usually fit you in without any issue. If you are slightly further afield, feel free to get in touch anyway and I will let you know if I can help.

finalCta.title: Want your hedges looking sharp again?
finalCta.description: Send me a quick description of your hedge, or a couple of photos showing the height and length, and I will quote the trim clearly. Most quotes come back within 24 hours.
